findings.title: Fire-and-forget legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes
findings.body: In Create (and similarly in Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) the async goroutine does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10*time.Second, ...)` using the `ctx` that was passed into the method, which is ultimately the HTTP request context. Go's net/http cancels the request context as soon as the handler (i.e. this Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection call and the rest of the request pipeline) returns and the response has been written. Since the goroutine is launched right before the function returns, in practice the derived context is cancelled almost immediately, well before the intended 10s timeout elapses, so the asynchronous write to legacy storage is very likely to be aborted mid-flight. This defeats the entire purpose of Mode 3's "write to legacy as a safety net" behavior: legacy will frequently fall out of sync without any visible error to the caller (errors are only logged/metriced inside the goroutine). The context used for the detached write should not inherit cancellation from the request (e.g. use `context.Background()` or `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` plus the desired timeout).

findings.title: Storage create failure is recorded as a legacy-duration metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. Legacy was never invoked on this path (the function returns before the async legacy call), so this mislabels a Storage failure as a Legacy failure, corrupting the dual-writer metrics used for monitoring/alerting.

findings.title: Storage update failure is recorded as a legacy-duration metric
findings.body: In `Update`, when `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. As with Create, Legacy.Update is never reached on this path, so the error is incorrectly attributed to the legacy backend instead of storage, making the dual-writer metrics misleading.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded under storage-duration metric
findings.body: Inside the async goroutine in `DeleteCollection`, after calling `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the result is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This mislabels the legacy call's duration/error as a storage metric, which is inconsistent with the equivalent code in Create/Delete/Update (which correctly use `recordLegacyDuration` for the legacy call) and corrupts observability data.

findings.title: Delete records the per-request object name as a Prometheus metric label instead of the resource kind
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object's `name` as the metric label where every other call site (Create, Get, List, Update, DeleteCollection, and the error branch just above at line 103) passes `options.Kind`. Using an effectively unbounded, per-object value (the resource name) as a Prometheus label value causes label cardinality to grow unboundedly with the number of distinct objects deleted, which can blow up memory/storage in the metrics backend and degrade or break querying. This is also inconsistent with every other metric label in this mode, making dashboards/alerts based on `kind` silently miss delete-success events.

findings.title: Delete puts the un-enriched base logger into the context instead of the locally built logger
findings.body: `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` is built but then `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` stores `d.Log` (without the added values) into the context, not the local `log` variable. Every other method in this file (Create, Get, List, Update, DeleteCollection) correctly stores the enriched `log`. As a result, any code downstream of `Delete` that retrieves the logger via `klog.FromContext(ctx)` loses the name/kind/method fields, making it harder to correlate logs for delete operations.

findings.title: Async legacy Update no longer uses the object actually written to Storage, risking divergence between stores
findings.body: The previous Mode3 implementation fetched the current object from Storage, computed the `updated` object once via `objInfo.UpdatedObject`, and explicitly wrapped that same computed object for both `Storage.Update` and `Legacy.Update` so both backends ended up with an identical payload. The new implementation calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` and then, in the detached goroutine, calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same raw `objInfo`. Since `objInfo.UpdatedObject` is invoked independently by each store (each using its own view of the "old" object), Legacy and Storage can end up computing and persisting different final objects, especially for patch-style updates. This undermines the stated goal of Mode 3 ("write to unified storage and then asynchronously write to legacy as a safety measure") because the legacy copy may not actually mirror what was stored in unified storage.

findings.title: No panic recovery in detached goroutines performing legacy writes
findings.body: The goroutines spawned in Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection (lines 50, 108, 134, 161) call into `d.Legacy.*` with no `recover()`. An unrecovered panic in any of these detached goroutines (e.g. triggered by a bug or unexpected state in a legacy store implementation) will crash the entire Grafana process, since Go terminates the program on an unhandled panic in any goroutine, not just the one serving the HTTP request. Fire-and-forget background work like this should guard against panics to avoid turning a legacy-storage bug into a full server crash.

findings.title: Mode3 tests never verify the asynchronous legacy writes actually occur
findings.body: The Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection tests configure `setupLegacyFn` mock expectations but the dual writer now performs the corresponding legacy write in a background goroutine. The tests return immediately after asserting on the synchronous result and never wait for the goroutine (no sync.WaitGroup, channel, or `require.Eventually`) nor call `m.AssertExpectations`/`AssertCalled` on the legacy mock. Consequently these tests would pass even if the goroutine were never launched, called the legacy store with wrong arguments, or if any of the metric-mislabeling bugs introduced in this PR regressed further — the new asynchronous behavior added by this PR is effectively untested.

findings.title: Duplicate checksum entry added for grafana/pkg/apimachinery go.mod
findings.body: The line `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod h1:DkxMin+qOh1Fgkxfbt+CUfBqqsCQJMG9op8Os/irBPA=` already existed in the file and is added again by this diff, producing a duplicate entry. This indicates `go.work.sum` was not regenerated cleanly (e.g. via `go mod tidy`/`go work sync`) and the unrelated dependency churn in this file (azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, otel packages, etc.) seems unrelated to the Mode 3 dual-writer feature described in the PR, suggesting it was accidentally bundled in from a different branch/rebase.
